text: Mamma, Sónya, look, it’s he!” “Who? Yes, on my word, it’s Bezúkhov!” said Natásha, putting her head out of the carriage and staring at a tall, stout man in a coachman’s long coat, who from his manner of walking and moving was evidently a gentleman in disguise, and who was passing under the arch of the Súkharev tower accompanied by a small, sallow-faced, beardless old man in a frieze coat. “Yes, it really is Bezúkhov in a coachman’s coat, with a queer-looking old boy. Really,” said Natásha, “look, look!” “No, it’s not he. How can you talk such nonsense?” “Mamma,” screamed Natásha, “I’ll stake my head it’s he!
